proof:
Source: parent proof, Part III (CL(0)), with the final appeal to T4 made through the sibling theorem cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (child im_local), whose hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) (the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub; not available to this child, hence assumed) are hypotheses here. For a 0-covector α write ⟨α⟩ := α(∅) (the value on the empty tuple); α ↦ ⟨α⟩ identifies Covector(ℝ^P, 0) with ℝ, and |α| = |⟨α⟩|. A 0-form a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) is identified with the smooth function x ↦ ⟨a(x)⟩.

1. Degree-0 IMReps. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) is the counting measure (μH[0]{x} = 1, Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U of S ∈ 𝒟_0(U). (i) For compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x∈M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ and θ ≥ 1 on M, so M ∩ K is finite. (ii) The only H⁰-null subset of M is ∅, so the orientation property of R holds at every x ∈ M: ξ(x) is a unit orientation of a 0-dimensional subspace; by the definition IsUnitOrientationOf with n = 0 (the orthonormal family is the empty family) ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)⟨α⟩ with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. (iii) Hence, with m(x) := ε(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, S(a) = Σ_{x∈M} m(x)⟨a(x)⟩ for a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (a finite sum: only x ∈ M ∩ tsupport a contribute). (iv) By (MR), for open G, M_G(S) = R.measure(G) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} θ(x) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} |m(x)|.
2. Locally finite mass of T. For open W ⊂⊂ U, M_W(T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(T_j) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) ≤ sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn is 0 in degree 0, and M_W(T_j) is bounded by the hypothesis).
3. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U. The open set B_{2r}(x₀) has compact closure in U, so c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞. Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) be IMReps of T_j and m_j as in step 1. By 1(iv), Σ_{x∈M_j∩B_{2r}(x₀)} |m_j(x)| ≤ c. Listing each x ∈ M_j ∩ B_{2r}(x₀) exactly |m_j(x)| times with sign ε_j(x): T_j(a) = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j} ε_{j,i}⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ for all a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_{2r}(x₀), where N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} ∈ {±1} and x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀).
4. N_j takes values in the finite set {0, …, ⌊c⌋} and (ε_{j,1}, …, ε_{j,N}) in the finite set {±1}^N, and B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N is compact; hence there is a subsequence (not relabeled; it still converges weakly to T) with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i ∈ B̄_{2r}(x₀) for i = 1, …, N.
5. For a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_r(x₀): T(a) = lim_j T_j(a) = lim_j Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(y_i)⟩ (a continuous). Let Y := {y_1, …, y_N}, m(y) := Σ_{i: y_i = y} ε_i ∈ ℤ for y ∈ Y and F := {y ∈ Y ∩ B_r(x₀) : m(y) ≠ 0}, a finite subset of B_r(x₀). Since a vanishes on Y ∖ B_r(x₀) (outside tsupport a), T(a) = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩.
6. The domain restriction T|_{B_r(x₀)} ∈ 𝒟_0(B_r(x₀)) is integer multiplicity. Define an IMRep in B_r(x₀): carrier F; mult(y) := |m(y)| for y ∈ F, 0 otherwise; orient(y)(α) := sign(m(y))⟨α⟩ for y ∈ F, orient(y) := 0 otherwise. F is finite, hence Borel; it is countably 0-rectifiable (each point is the range of a constant, hence Lipschitz, map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P; SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range and countablyRectifiable_iUnion); mult and orient take finitely many values on finitely many points, so they are Borel/strongly measurable; mult > 0 on F; ∫_{F∩K} mult dH⁰ ≤ Σ_{y∈F}|m(y)| < ∞. Orientation at y ∈ F: the subspace {0} has finrank 0 and, with δ := dist(y, F ∖ {y}) > 0 (δ := ∞ if F = {y}), for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and 0 < ρ < δ/R_f, the blow-up blowUpMap y ρ (F) = ρ⁻¹(F − y) meets tsupport f at most in 0, so ∫_{blowUpMap y ρ '' F} f dH⁰ = f(0) = ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰; thus HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y {0}, and orient(y) = ±⟨·⟩ is a unit orientation of {0} (IsUnitOrientationOf with the empty orthonormal family). Representation: for a ∈ 𝒟^0(B_r(x₀)), the action is Σ_{y∈F} |m(y)| sign(m(y))⟨a(y)⟩ = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩ = T(a) = T|_{B_r(x₀)}(a) by step 5.
7. Steps 3–6 apply to every x₀ ∈ U (with some r > 0, B_r(x₀) ⊆ U). Together with step 2, part (1) of the sibling theorem cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (applied with the hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC)) shows that T is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: Degree-0 IMReps are locally finite point sets with integer weights m(x) ≠ 0 (H⁰ is counting measure, orientations ±1), and by (MR) M_G = Σ|m| on open G.
T has locally finite mass by lower semicontinuity.
On B_{2r}(x₀) each T_j is a sum of at most c signed Dirac masses; pass to a subsequence with constant count and signs and convergent points.
On B_r(x₀), T equals a finite integer combination of Dirac masses, which is IM (explicit IMRep, approximate tangent space {0}).
